name: Bulk-available declassified document corpora (CREST, NARA, JFK, Black Vault, NSArchive, DOE OpenNet)

preservation.reason: This record catalogs external corpora without forking or mutating them. Foundry owns source discovery; SISO Knowledge holds durable corpus; Evidence Engines perform source-grounded transformation; the Great Library stays a catalog and lineage surface, not a warehouse. Nothing is dirty: the bytes live upstream; this record catalogs the catalog and the rights posture.

source_scopes.name: NARA AWS Catalog and JFK bulk downloads
The Black Vault curated FOIA archive (link-only pending permission)

campaign.objective: Acquire and preserve bulk-available declassified document corpora for analysis and durable citation in SISO Works.

units.name: CIA CREST archive mirror on Internet Archive (four-torrent split)
units.rationale: The four-torrent bundle is 528.7 GB covering 934,739 documents and approximately 12 million pages, including the Stargate collection; items are US Government work under Public Domain Mark 1.0. This bulk route is cheaper than scraping cia.gov/readingroom, whose robots policy imposes a 10-second crawl delay and disallows search endpoints.

evidence.summary: Item page lists 195.5G, 250,000 declassified files from CIA's CREST archive, Part 1 of 4, with TAR, CSV and torrent files, and Public Domain Mark 1.0.
Item page lists 90.9G and 250,000 declassified CREST documents, Part 2 of 4, with the same bulk archive shape.
Item page lists 66.9G and 250,000 declassified CREST documents, Part 3 of 4.
Item page lists 175.4G and 184,739 declassified CREST documents, Part 4 of 4; the four parts total 934,739 documents and 528.7 GB.

The item metadata identifies the files as US Government work and displays Public Domain Mark 1.0; bulk bundles are scanned PDFs without an OCR text layer, while per-RDP items have OCR and DocumentCloud hosts an OCR'd copy.

units.name: National Archives Catalog dataset on AWS (anonymous S3 sync)
units.target: external upstream mirror (NARA AWS Open Data)
units.rationale: The dataset contains 261 GB of metadata and URLs for over 148 million digital objects, bypassing the 10,000-per-month API ceiling and enabling scripted bulk fetches. Federal materials are generally public domain, but not every catalog item is guaranteed so item-level rights remain required.

evidence.summary: NARA documentation states the dataset contains over 261 gigabytes of data and URLs for over 148 million digital objects as of 2026-03-01.
The documentation provides an anonymous S3 sync command for s3://nara-national-archives-catalog/.
NARA states the Catalog API exists but explicitly forbids scraping the catalog through it.
NARA privacy guidance explains federal materials are generally public domain while not guaranteeing that every item has unrestricted rights.

units.name: JFK Assassination Records Collection bulk-download ZIPs (2017–2025 tranches)
units.rationale: NARA publishes direct tranche ZIPs with MD5 checksums across 2017–2018, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025 releases. The collection exceeds six million pages; per-page document count and total GB remain unconfirmed, although tranche sizes of 1.2G, 12.7G, 339M and 5.2G are receipted.

evidence.summary: The official bulk-download page exposes direct catalog.archives.gov/medialz/bulk-downloads/jfk ZIP URLs and MD5 checksums for the published tranches.
NARA reports 2,672 documents posted during April–June 2023 and lists tranche sizes including 1.2G, 12.7G, 339M and 5.2G.
NARA describes over six million pages of records, photographs, motion pictures, sound recordings and artifacts in the JFK collection.

units.name: DeclassDB CREST mirror (OCR'd subset)
units.rationale: DeclassDB OCRs 309,708 of approximately 934,000 CREST documents, providing full-text search where the Internet Archive torrents do not. It is a search-index layer rather than a complete mirror; semantic search is paid and PDFs link to government sites.

evidence.summary: The CREST page states 309,708 records, 1.05M pages and full-text OCR; result pages are capped at 500.

units.name: DocumentCloud CREST upload by MuckRock
units.rationale: MuckRock's DocumentCloud upload provides an OCR'd, queryable hosted copy of approximately one million files and 13 million pages. The REST API supports bulk POST /api/documents/ but requires DocumentCloud credentials.

evidence.summary: MuckRock states it forced release of 13 million pages (one million files) from the CIA CREST archive.

units.name: DOE OpenNet (declassified nuclear documents, OSTI)
units.rationale: OpenNet exposes 485,000+ bibliographic references and 140,000+ full-text declassified documents. The material is public-domain US government work, but DOE/NARA periodically withdraw records that contain improperly declassified Restricted Data or Formerly Restricted Data, requiring re-checks against the live index.

evidence.summary: OSTI states OpenNet contains 485,000+ bibliographic references and 140,000 declassified documents.
OSTI identifies the declassified US government documents as public domain and warns that records may be withdrawn when RD/FRD is discovered.

units.name: The Black Vault curated FOIA document archive (link_existing pending permission)
units.rationale: The Black Vault reports 3,861,432 pages across 11,000+ FOIA requests and has real curatorial value layered over public-domain material. Do not bulk mirror without explicit permission from John Greenewald: the site exposes no redistribution policy and carries a commercial copyright notice. If permission is granted, the Stargate ZIP is a high-value acquisition: 6.61 GB, 89,901 pages and 12,301 files.

evidence.summary: The archive page reports Current Government Document Page Count Within The Black Vault: 3,861,432.
The footer displays © 2026 The Black Vault, Inc.; no bulk redistribution grant or terms of use were located.
The Stargate package is listed as a 6.61 GB ZIP containing 89,901 pages across 12,301 files.
robots.txt permits AI crawlers including GPTBot, ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai; this is supportive access evidence, not permission to redistribute.

units.name: National Security Archive (George Washington University) free-site documents
units.rationale: The free site provides 790+ e-books and 10,000+ declassified documents under a nonexclusive limited license requiring attribution and link-back. Never mirror ProQuest's commercially licensed DNSA, which covers 104,000+ documents across 60 subscription collections.

evidence.summary: The site distinguishes subscription DNSA as ProQuest's paywalled resource covering more than 104,000 curated primary-source documents, while the free site offers 790+ e-books and 10,000+ declassified documents under a nonexclusive limited license; US government work is not claimed by copyright.

units.name: governmentattic.org (FOIA documents aggregated)
units.rationale: This self-funded First Amendment site aggregates thousands of FOIA documents, but exposes no bulk endpoint or torrent. Robots policy is unverified, so obtain permission before aggressive crawling.

evidence.summary: The site describes itself as a First Amendment free speech website containing electronic copies of thousands of Federal Government documents obtained under FOIA.

units.name: CIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room (per-document fetch via official UI)
units.rationale: The Stargate collection is paginated across at least 291 pages. Use per-document fetch through the official UI only: robots.txt disallows search endpoints and sets Crawl-delay: 10. The Internet Archive torrents cover the bulk case at lower cost.

evidence.summary: CIA robots.txt disallows /readingroom/search/, /advanced-search-view/ and /request/, and specifies Crawl-delay: 10.
The Stargate collection UI is paginated and page=291 was observed; documents are fetched individually.
CIA identifies the collection as US Government work; the underlying declassified documents are public domain.
NARA's official dataset page reports over 261 GB and URLs for over 148 million digital objects and documents anonymous S3 synchronization.
The IA CREST-1 receipt lists 195.5G and 250,000 declassified files from the CIA CREST archive, Part 1 of 4, with TAR/CSV/torrent distribution and Public Domain Mark 1.0.
UK National Archives Discovery developer terms were reviewed for caching and reuse constraints; no caching clause was found in the reviewed terms.

This inventory follows the proven Gutenberg precedent: schema_version 1.0.0, omitted inventory_kind, source_scopes, units with evidence, and the rationale that Foundry owns source discovery while the Great Library remains a catalog rather than a warehouse.
